_readme: Committed p95 latency budgets for the nightly-load-test CI job (#1082). See docs/development/nightly-load-test.md for the full contract: fixture size, budget-derivation rule, and how to re-derive this file at each release. DO NOT hand-edit budget_p95_ms to a round number — every value here must trace to a measured_p95_ms via the stated formula.
status_note: Re-derived 2026-11-25 (#2430, #2195, #2237, #2538) from job 18346366386 -- the 2026-11-25 scheduled nightly-load-test run on main at f22f8d19a on gitlab-runner-nuc-3-visiban (tag nuc), pipeline 3111903584. Every p95 budget is ceil(measured_p95_ms * 1.4 / 5) * 5 and every peak-RSS budget is ceil(measured_peak_rss_mb * 1.4 / 5) * 5 from that one artifact, whole file in one pass; measured_peak_rss_mb is the artifact's peak_rss_mb, kept next to its budget so the memory figure traces. All 42 scenarios were in the artifact and the job passed with --server-pid-file, so nothing in this file is pending any more: the aged-board, linked-board, overview and fan-out scenarios (#2430), the gate-row scenarios (#2195, #2237) and children_view (#2538) all have committed p95 and peak-RSS budgets, and the pending_budget / pending_memory_budget keys are gone. This is a single run on the 4-generation aged fixture (9,640 archived cards, about 1 year of history); the nightly never runs the 12-generation (3-year) fixture or DEBUG=False, so there is no committed budget for one overview open on 3 years of history (see the Exit run section of the doc). Run-to-run spread of the two preceding scheduled runs (jobs 18307746300 on 2026-11-24 and 18268136113 on 2026-11-23, same fixture, 40-41 of the 42 scenarios present): the max/min p95 ratio across the three runs has a median of 1.09 and is at most 1.15 for 31 of 40 scenarios; the widest are board_movements_deep (101.5 to 161.4ms), card_search (67.0 to 97.9ms), flow_wip_age (358.2 to 476.5ms) and flow_dwell. Peak RSS of this run is 0.5 to 39.4MB above the lowest of the three. No p95 or peak RSS from either earlier run exceeds the budgets below. History: 2026-11-19 (#2110, #2237, #2063) from job 18170442650 on gitlab-runner-nuc-2-visiban; 2026-10-21 (#1808) from job 17348200339 on gitlab-runner-nuc-2-visiban; 2026-10-20 (#1767) from job 17304593759 on runner-04-NUC; 2026-09-30 (#1233) from job 16796708105. Peak RSS is measured with DEBUG=True under runserver --noreload, so it is higher than a production pod's; the budget moves with the code, not with production. Re-derive again at the next release per docs/development/nightly-load-test.md#re-deriving-the-baseline.

fixture.note: --scale 20 replicates the 10-swimlane demo layout 20x (11-13 cards/swimlane, same distribution as the normal demo board) rather than picking an arbitrary target card count directly. The load-test board has 20 members (5 demo users + 15 loadtest* filler accounts, #1723).
fixture.multi_board_note: #1810: --extra-boards 199 adds 199 small boards (8 cards each, 1,592 cards) owned by demo3, so demo3 can access 200 boards with the load-test board. The extra boards belong to demo3 alone, so the demo1 board_list and demo2 scenarios see the same boards as before. Every measured_p95_ms in this file was taken with the extra boards present (#1808).
fixture.aged_and_linked: #2430/#2424: seed_demo_data also gets --aged-generations N and --linked-boards. Both fixtures live on boards only the loadtest_analytics user can open, so what viewers can see is unchanged. Row counts grow (cards about 4k to about 16.5k, movements about 5x, with the aged fixture on; --linked-boards adds about 525 more cards and the children-view fixture about 50,500, so about 67.5k, #2538; the load-test board also gets gate rows and "Doing" sub-columns, #2405), so the existing budgets may move: expected, not proven (as #1810). The isolation is about board access, not authorship (demo1-5 still author and are assigned the aged cards). Known limit: aged copies carry movements only, no CardBlock history, and blocked_at/due_date are not shifted, so aged_flow_blocked is not an aged-history measurement.

measurement_method.percentile_method: nearest-rank (no interpolation) over the 40 timed samples
measurement_method.auth: manage.py provision_fuzz_token --username demo2 (scoped, non-admin PAT; board_list alone authenticates as the board owner demo1 via --owner-token-file — same mechanism backend-schema-fuzz already uses)

budget_formula: budget_p95_ms = ceil(measured_p95_ms * 1.4 / 5) * 5 -- a 1.4x factor (issue #1082 specifies 1.3-1.5x) rounded up to the nearest 5ms so CI comparisons have a little headroom for measurement noise without the number itself being picked round. Recompute this whole file -- never hand-adjust a single budget_p95_ms -- when re-deriving.

board_list.note: Board list as the board OWNER (demo1, via --owner-token-file) so the access query spans the 20-member board; member_count/card_count/archived_card_count are independent correlated subqueries (#1723).

board_full.note: Serializes the entire board (all 2388 cards) in one response, unpaginated -- the most volume-sensitive endpoint in the fixture and the one this budget is least tolerant of relative headroom on, since a regression here is the one TruePPM's #2767 postmortem describes (index-shape regression, identical query count, higher latency). Also the most CPU-bound of the six (per-card DRF field serialization across ~2,388 cards, #1212), so it shows the most run-to-run variance on a shared CI runner -- expect wider swings here than on the lighter endpoints below.

card_search.note: The cross-board card query as a one-board user (demo2): access filter plus one 51-row cursor page. Card search now filters with the ci_contains lookup (ILIKE on PostgreSQL), which the pg_trgm GIN indexes from migration 0030 (card_title_trgm_idx / card_desc_trgm_idx) can serve for selective terms (#1809). The budget was re-derived from NUC job 18170442650 and broad/short terms re-measured in #2063 (plans in docs/development/nightly-load-test.md). Derived after the #1805 fix (#1808). 'the' is a deliberately broad, high-cardinality search term -- it matches a large fraction of the corpus, closer to a real user's search-as-you-type behavior than a highly selective term would be.

card_search_multi_board.note: The same query as card_search, run as demo3, who can access 200 boards, so the card SELECT filters on a 200-id literal list. PostgreSQL is expected to scan the matching cards and sort instead of walking card_board_updated_idx (#1805 measured 13.5ms vs 0.65ms execution on the one-board fixture; this fixture layout was not EXPLAINed, so the plan is expected, not confirmed). Budget derived from a NUC run in #1808.

card_timeline.note: Unified movement + activity feed for a single card. Exercises the comment_card_created_idx / activity_card_created_idx composite indexes added in migration 0045. NOTE (#2365, #2405): the timeline also returns gate entries. The fixture now seeds a gated stage with gate rows (about two thirds of its active cards, some linked to a move, some not) and the script reads a card that passed a gate, but the budget below was derived on the run that includes the gate rows (#2430).

card_timeline_counts.note: The card detail sheet's request (#967): the timeline page plus the per-group counts queries, on every card open and every card.version change.

card_list.note: Board card list, default 200-row cap with X-Total-Count/X-Truncated. Page read without a window count; a full page adds one bare COUNT (#2239).

cards_archived.note: First archived-cards page (50 rows). Page read without a window count; a full page adds one bare COUNT on the archived_at index (#2239).

board_movements.note: Board History first page (50 rows, newest first). Page query on the (board, -moved_at) index plus a bare COUNT, no window count (#1961).

board_movements_deep.note: Board History at a deep offset, derived from the first page's count at run time.

board_movements_dated.note: Board History with the date filter, a half-open datetime range on moved_at instead of a __date cast (#1961).

notifications_list.note: The frontend polls this every 15-30s (visiban/settings.py's DEFAULT_THROTTLE_RATES comment) -- the highest-QPS authenticated endpoint in the product, even though its own per-request cost is capped at 50 rows by NotificationListView.

notifications_unread.note: Companion to notifications_list -- polled at the same interval; unlike the list it is uncapped (counts all accessible unread rows).

board_summary.note: Per-swimlane counts plus a replay of the cards that entered a done column in the last 30 days (#448). Before #448 this was SQL aggregates only.

board_analytics.note: Heatmap, stalled cards and blocked time, with a replay of the cards relevant to the default 30-day window plus the frozen avg_days_per_column prefetch (#448).

flow_cycle_time.note: Replays every movement of the fixture board in Python (one query), then samples completions in the default 90-day range (#448).

flow_throughput.note: Same replay as flow_cycle_time, bucketed into whole ISO weeks (#448).

flow_cumulative_flow.note: Same replay; 90 days x columns from a difference array, never a per-day query (#448).

flow_wip_age.note: Same replay plus one query each for block rows and blocking relations (#448).

flow_dwell.note: Same replay as cumulative flow, then completed dwell percentiles per column (#2260).

flow_blocked.note: Same replay plus block rows and blocking relations (#2260).

flow_attention.note: Same replay plus blocking relations and the card directory (#2260).

flow_swimlanes.note: Same replay as cycle time plus block rows, bucketed per swimlane (#2266).

flow_overview.note: The one request the Analytics overview makes for its seven flow charts since #2426 (days=90&limit=300, as the overview sends it since #2429): one history load instead of seven.

aged_board_summary.note: Aged board (#2430): the load-test board's shape plus archived generations, 90 days apart.

aged_flow_cumulative_flow_day.note: Aged board (#2430): the cumulative-flow day drill-down 540 days back, mid-history (#2444).

aged_flow_overview.note: Aged board (#2430): the overview's single flow request (#2426) on years of archived history.

linked_board_full.note: Linked child board (#2424): 500 cards, each with a parent on one of 5 parent boards.

linked_card_list.note: Linked child board (#2424): 500 cards, each with a parent on one of 5 parent boards.

analytics_overview.path: 2 reads at once, each with ?days=90&limit=300 as the overview sends (#2426, #2429): metrics/overview/ and analytics/ on the load-test board
analytics_overview.note: The overview open on the active-only board (#2430). Since #2426 the overview fires two reads (metrics/overview/ for the seven flow charts, analytics/ for the heatmap); wall time to the last response, peak RSS of the one server process.

aged_analytics_overview.path: the same 2 reads (metrics/overview/ and analytics/), each with ?days=90&limit=300, on the aged board
aged_analytics_overview.note: The overview open on the aged board (#2430). Since #2426 the overview fires two reads (metrics/overview/ for the seven flow charts, analytics/ for the heatmap); wall time to the last response, peak RSS of the one server process.

children_view.note: Children mode's first page (#2370) on a parent board with 500 parents, about 100 children each (#2538). The endpoint recomputes every live link on the board per page with correlated subqueries, so one request is O(parents x children) and scrolling the board is that cost times the page count; the query-count tests cannot see it. If its p95 or peak RSS is out of proportion, whether the per-page recompute should become per-lane or cached is the open question #2538 owns.
